summary: The core video player embedded across web, mobile, and TV apps, handling playback, buffering, and DRM licensing for every stream.
Adjusts video quality in real time based on the viewer's network conditions to minimize rebuffering without wasting bandwidth on unnecessary resolution.
Lets subscribers download titles to their device for offline viewing, enforcing expiration windows tied to their license terms.
Keeps playback position, watchlist, and preferences in sync across every device a viewer uses to watch the same account.
Mirrors a live broadcast feed to the streaming app in near real time, with a chat overlay for viewers watching the simulcast.
Stores and organizes every video, image, and script asset used in production, with version history and approval status per asset.
Moves a finished piece of content through review, legal clearance, and scheduled publish steps, notifying each stakeholder at their stage.
Tracks every edit made to an article or show description, letting editors roll back to a prior version if a change needs reverting.
Coordinates subtitle and dubbing work across languages for each title, tracking which markets still need translated assets before launch.
Gives editors a shared calendar of upcoming publish dates across every show and article, flagging scheduling conflicts before they happen.
Stitches ad breaks directly into the video stream on the server side, avoiding client-side ad blockers and reducing playback stutter at ad boundaries.
Limits how many times a given viewer sees the same ad within a session or day, keeping ad experiences from feeling repetitive.
Runs a real-time bidding auction among demand partners for each available ad slot and serves the winning creative within the bid deadline.
Rotates multiple creative variants for the same campaign to prevent ad fatigue and to feed performance data back to the advertiser.
Screens content for brand safety categories before ad slots are sold against it, keeping advertiser creative away from flagged content.
Reports minutes watched, unique viewers, and completion rate per title, updated hourly for the content team's daily standups.
Scores subscribers on likelihood to cancel based on declining watch time, feeding a retention offer campaign before they lapse.
Shows exactly where in an episode viewers drop off or rewind, helping producers see which scenes hold attention and which don't.
Lets analysts build custom viewer cohorts by signup date or genre preference and compare their retention curves side by side.
Shows how many viewers are watching a live event right now, broken down by region, used by ops to watch for streaming capacity issues.
Builds the personalized rows of title recommendations shown on the home screen, ranked by each viewer's watch history and ratings.
Asks new viewers to rate a handful of titles during signup and uses those answers to bootstrap recommendations before watch history exists.
Powers the "more like this" rail on a title's detail page by finding catalog titles with similar genre, cast, and viewing patterns.
Keeps the continue-watching rail accurate across devices, removing a title once it's finished and reordering by most recently watched.
Lets the editorial team manually pin or boost specific titles in the recommendation rails for promotional campaigns and premieres.
Lets a live director cut between camera feeds, graphics, and pre-recorded packages during a live broadcast from a single control surface.
Generates near-real-time closed captions for a live broadcast using speech recognition, with a human editor able to correct errors on the fly.
Routes feeds from dozens of remote cameras at a live event into the production truck, letting the switcher select any feed instantly.
Lets a replay operator mark and cue up highlight moments during a live sports broadcast for instant playback from any camera angle.
Drives the lower-third, scoreboard, and ticker graphics overlaid on a live broadcast, pulling live data feeds for scores and stats.
Lets subscribers upgrade, downgrade, or pause their plan and shows the prorated billing impact of the change before they confirm it.
Retries failed subscription renewal charges on a staggered schedule and emails the subscriber to update their payment method before cancellation.
Manages free trial eligibility and conversion tracking, preventing the same household from repeatedly claiming a new trial.
Lets a primary subscriber add household profiles to a shared family plan, each with its own watch history and parental controls.
Targets recently canceled subscribers with a time-limited discount offer to win them back before they forget about the service entirely.
Screens user comments for harassment and spam before they post, holding borderline cases for human moderator review.
Queues newly uploaded user-generated videos for moderator review against community guidelines before they're published publicly.
Fingerprints uploaded video against a database of copyrighted content and flags matches for the rights holder to claim or dispute.
Samples frames and audio from active livestreams to catch policy violations while a broadcast is still in progress, not after the fact.
Lets creators appeal a moderation decision and gives a second-line reviewer the original content and first decision to reconsider.
Lets show producers upload an episode, add show notes, and schedule its release time across every distribution feed at once.
Generates and maintains the podcast RSS feed for each show, keeping it valid against the directories that consume it.
Reports downloads, listen-through rate, and audience geography per episode so producers can see which segments hold listeners.
Inserts targeted ad spots into episode audio at request time, letting older episodes carry fresh, geo-targeted sponsorships.
Automatically transcribes each episode and publishes a searchable transcript alongside the audio for accessibility and SEO.
Tracks the terms of every content licensing agreement, including territory, window, and renewal date, in one searchable ledger.
Determines which countries a title is licensed to stream in and automatically geo-restricts playback outside those territories.
Calculates royalty payments owed to rights holders based on streams and licensing terms, generating the statements finance pays against.
Schedules when a licensed title becomes available or must be pulled from the catalog based on its contracted licensing window.
Tracks talent and music clearance status for original productions, blocking a title from publishing until every clearance is confirmed.
Gives independent creators a browser-based studio to upload, trim, and add captions to their videos before publishing to the platform.
Shows creators watch time, subscriber growth, and revenue per video in a single dashboard tailored to their own channel.
Lets creators enable ads, fan subscriptions, and tipping on their channel and see a combined payout summary each month.
Lets creators invite another channel to co-publish a video and automatically splits revenue and analytics between both accounts.
Runs an A/B test between two thumbnail options on a live video and automatically promotes the one that gets a higher click-through rate.
Lets catalog operators edit a title's cast, synopsis, and rating information, keeping every storefront in sync with a single source of truth.
Suggests genre and mood tags for newly ingested titles using automated content analysis, which catalogers can confirm or override.
Manages the different key art crops and thumbnails a title needs across devices and locales, validating each meets size requirements.
Publishes and unpublishes catalog titles automatically according to their licensed availability window without manual catalog edits.
Rebuilds the catalog search index from the latest metadata each night so new titles and corrections show up in on-platform search the next morning.
